hoist up operator+injured.#comment: With the hoist out the operator and the patient stay on the hook (HOIST_OUT 1): the baseline speed, bank and load ladders of Hoisting back up take over. Otherwise they are aboard.

custom injured assets prepare.#comment: Models of the injured chosen by the custom script (train.json, local CUS_INJURED: array of structures {title, sex, age, var1, var2}, in the order of the injured). Runs once per dispatch from objective2, after accident demographics sex and before the pathology engine, only in a custom mission (player custom) and not on a reload. The pick is always cleared first, so a list of a previous dispatch never survives. Empty or absent list: nothing changes. Fewer entries than injured (HELOVICTIMS): the pick is the list in order, the remaining injured keep the choice of the mission. As many: the list in order. More entries than injured: HELOVICTIMS entries drawn at random, each list entry at most once. The pick is cus_injured_pick (an array of the entries, with idx when drawn); custom injured entry reads it.

custom injured entry.#comment: Reads the pick of the injured of param slot (1 to 3) into cie_title, cie_sex, cie_age, cie_var1, cie_var2 (null when the slot has no entry or the field is missing).

custom injured demographics sex.#comment: Sex of the injured chosen by the user (entry field sex, male or female, lowercase; anything else leaves the sex of the mission). Runs right after accident demographics sex, so that the pathology engine picks profiles of that sex. The user wins over the wording of the dispatch.

custom injured demographics ages.#comment: Age of the injured chosen by the user (entry field age, a number). Runs right after accident demographics ages, so the user wins over the range of the dispatch and over the age of a pathology profile. A field that is not a number leaves the age of the mission.

custom injured fallback.#comment: Fallback model of a custom injured title: the title can be misspelled or not installed, and create_object then takes its fallback_title. The fallback is drawn at random from the static injured_fallback (the H145 injured models of the mission) and is a different one for each injured while the list has enough entries (cus_fb_picked holds the ones already given, cleared when the list is used up). Result in cus_fb_title.

custom injured asset.#comment: Applies the pick of custom injured assets prepare to one injured (param slot 1 to 3), from random injured, before the creation: the title replaces injuredN, var_compatibleN comes from the catalog of the mission when the title is in one of its lists (injured, injured_workers, injured_motorcyclists) and is no (fixed model, the safe answer) for a title the mission does not know, the fallback of a title that is misspelled or not installed is drawn from injured_fallback. SEXn and AGEn are set again from the entry (a workers mission puts male in SEX1 while it chooses the model). No entry for the slot: nothing changes.

custom injured vars.#comment: VAR 1 and VAR 2 of an injured chosen by the user (entry fields var1 and var2: NO or a missing field leaves what the mission does, a number is set). Runs right after the creation of the injured (param slot 1 to 3), after the mission has set VAR 1 to 0. Later events of the mission can change the state again.

clock now.#comment: The clock chosen in the dispatch control page: CLOCK_MODE local gives the simulator local time (E:LOCAL TIME, suffix L), anything else the simulator UTC (E:ZULU TIME, suffix Z). CLOCK_NOW_S is the whole seconds since midnight and CLOCK_SUFFIX the letter.

eta clock.#comment: Arrival time of a vehicle as a time of day on the chosen clock (see clock now): the clock plus the travel time in seconds, wrapped at midnight, in ETA_CLOCK; the letter is in CLOCK_SUFFIX. It is shown with the TIME format.

record patient death time.#comment: Time of death of patients 1 to 3 (seconds since midnight on the clock chosen in the dispatch control page, shown with the TIME format and the clock letter), kept in a local at the death (registry events) or at the first visit or display of the dead patient, and shown in the medical page. The first value wins.

post dispatcher message.#comment: Posts one message in the RescueTrack list; the list entry carries the time, so it is also the log. The sender is chosen by the optional param from: crew is the helicopter crew reporting to the dispatcher (-OUT-), fire, police and ambulance are the units on scene (their call signs firename, poliname, ambuname), anything else is the dispatcher (GRPNAME). A message belongs to whoever knows the fact: the dispatcher only posts what it decides or what it was told by a crew or a unit before.

SAR dispatcher text.#comment: Search and rescue: the dispatcher update carries only what the people who report can know: number, age and sex. No consciousness, symptoms or pathology (user request of 2026-10-18). Called after each update text, before the deceased note.

accident demographics sex.#comment: Sex of patient 1 by the wording of the dispatch (user request 2026-10-18): the static accident demographics (by ID_CARD, field sexN for the variant CRASH_VARIABLE) is put in SEX1 before the pathology engine, like injured_workers; the engine then takes only the profiles of that sex. A saved game keeps what it saved.

accident demographics ages.#comment: Ages of the patients by the activity of the dispatch (user request 2026-10-18): age_min and age_max of the accident (age_minN and age_maxN for the variant CRASH_VARIABLE win) bring AGE1, AGE2 and AGE3 into range after the pathology engine (the profile of patient 1 can set an age of its own). Only the patients that exist; a saved game keeps its ages.

symptoms parts.#comment: Medical update of the ambulance (user request 2026-10-18): the symptoms are told only when they are known. The profiles with NO INFO say nothing, and the same text is used for every patient (patients 2 and 3 used the name of the pathology as symptoms).

manual transport check.#comment: Transport choice of a manual visit (rules of the owner, 2026-11-20, after the talk with Dr.DougRoss). The player may make the mistake and the consequences follow: GROUND is possible for any patient while an ambulance on scene is still free (one patient per ambulance), HEMS for one patient only (never two by helicopter). Combinations: 1 patient either; 2 patients one HEMS and one GROUND, or both GROUND; 3 patients one HEMS and two GROUND, or all three GROUND (the HEMS crew returns to the helicopter). A patient who is not stable (SpO2 < 90, HR outside 50-120, GCS < 8, L:HEALTH 1) is recommended HEMS: GROUND for him counts an error and costs Life Score. The helicopter reserve and the live ground suitability follow the manual choice. Writes medical_display_ground_ok / _reason, medical_display_hems_ok / _reason and manual_pN_transport_recommend (param patient 1-3).
